evidence.text: Analyze normalizable radial modes in hard-wall AdS using Bessel functions and an illustrative Dirichlet IR condition. Large operator dimensions give heavier four-dimensional resonances; a semiclassical string falling to the IR wall supplies a complementary redshift argument.

evidence.text: Voigt-profile fitting with vpfit minimizes χ² simultaneously across species. Velocity structure is finalized before introducing Δα/α as a free parameter; isotopic and hyperfine structure are included where available and appropriate.

Resonance frequency, phase and decay time are monitored experimentally.

sources.title: Instantons and wormholes in Minkowski and (A)dS spaces

evidence.text: When do Euclidean instantons and nonsingular, finite-action wormholes exist in d-dimensional axion-dilaton gravity with zero, negative or positive cosmological constant, and how does existence depend on the dilaton coupling?

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes in string theory

evidence.text: Can the axion and dilaton fields of a string compactification support a smooth Euclidean throat? The relevant classical equations use an indefinite scalar metric obtained by continuing the axionic variables while retaining ordinary dilaton kinetic signs.

sources.title: Inviolable energy conditions from entanglement inequalities

evidence.text: Which necessary constraints on nonlinear bulk geometries follow from strong subadditivity and positivity/monotonicity of boundary relative entropy, and how can Einstein's equations express these constraints as energy conditions?

sources.title: The rigid Horowitz-Myers conjecture

evidence.text: Assuming the Riemannian Horowitz-Myers mass bound, must a metric attaining the proposed minimum be a Horowitz-Myers geon? The paper tests this through conditional scalar-curvature rigidity and reduction to static uniqueness.

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes, baby universes, and their impact on particle physics and cosmology

evidence.text: Does quantum gravity permit low-energy topology change in four and higher dimensions, and what determines the resulting baby-universe state? If it forbids these processes, a censorship mechanism and alternative UV-independent axionic symmetry-breaking objects are needed.

evidence.text: Can ordinary charged quantum fields support a parametrically controlled, traversable four-dimensional wormhole without creating a shortcut through ambient space, and can its mouths and throat remain metastable?

evidence.text: How much information can traverse a Gao–Jafferis–Wall wormhole while a controlled semiclassical bulk description remains valid, despite its very short opening, and how does this depend on black-hole size, species number and transverse localization?

sources.title: Swampland, Gradient Flow and Infinite Distance

evidence.text: Can an anisotropic, non-Einstein geometric flow reproduce a logarithmic infinite-distance limit and activate a radius modulus that would not flow on an isolated flat circle?

sources.title: Infinite Black Hole Entropies at Infinite Distances and Tower of States

evidence.text: Does a curvature-based distance between black-hole metrics depend on the radial coordinate used to compare them? The supplied calculation contrasts dimensionful and dimensionless radial descriptions.

sources.title: An Alliance in the Tripartite Conflict over Moduli Space

evidence.text: Do metrics constructed from symplectic geometry, slow-motion dynamics, and spacetime metric variations assign the same distance to a limit with a deepening gravitational throat and light states?

sources.title: Wormhole Renormalization: The gravitational path integral, holography, and a gauge group for topology change

evidence.text: Can effects of unknown microscopic wormholes be parametrized recursively, analogously to renormalization counterterms, to restore holographic factorization? What Hopf algebra and topology-changing group organize equivalent gravitational path-integral prescriptions?

sources.title: Navigating string theory field space with geometric flows

evidence.text: Can geometric flows probe infinite-distance limits in scalar field spaces with flux-induced potentials, and extend the Ricci Flow Conjecture beyond metric–dilaton backgrounds without explicitly deriving the compactified potential?

sources.title: There is no R**3 x S**1 vacuum gravitational instanton

evidence.text: Can a nonflat vacuum gravitational instanton exist on R^3 × S^1 with asymptotically flat noncompact directions and a fixed Euclidean period only near infinity?

sources.title: Non-extremal instantons and wormholes in string theory

evidence.text: Which non-extremal, spherically symmetric Euclidean gravity–dilaton–axion solutions exist, when are they completely regular wormholes, and can such wormholes occur in Calabi–Yau compactifications of string theory?

sources.title: The Riemannian manifold of all Riemannian metrics

evidence.text: What are the connection, curvature, geodesics, exponential mapping and Jacobi fields of the infinite-dimensional manifold of Riemannian metrics with its canonical weak integral metric, including when the underlying manifold is noncompact?

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes in string theory

evidence.text: Fourier project onto charges before extremizing, vary endpoint values as integration variables, solve the resulting complex equations, and retain all boundary terms in the weight. For wormholes, only dilatons must interpolate continuously between the specified physical end data.

sources.title: Inviolable energy conditions from entanglement inequalities

evidence.text: Conserved momenta associated with bulk Killing vectors give variations of geodesic length under endpoint changes. For spatial intervals, the derivative with respect to interval size measures the minimum spatial scale factor reached by the RT surface.

sources.title: The rigid Horowitz-Myers conjecture

evidence.text: Solve the asymptotic Yamabe problem to restore R=−n(n−1). Boundary expansions and maximum-principle barriers establish a strict mass decrease when the initial scalar curvature is nonconstant, contradicting the assumed minimum.
